newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler buys distribution rights, denies Rover rumors. [CORRECTED 22:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Chrysler buys distribution rights, denies Rover rumors. [CORRECTED 22:15 GMT]

text.p: Chrysler Corp. has reacquired distribution rights for its products in Germany, the Netherlands and Belgium from the Louwman Group, the companies said Tuesday.
In the past 18 months, Chrysler has acquired distribution rights in Austria, Argentina, Brazil, France, Italy and Japan.

Under the agreement in principle, Louwman will sell Chrysler Import Deutschland, Chrysler Import Holland, Chrysler Import Belgium and Public Warehouse Europe to Chrysler International Corp. as operating entities.
The deal is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter, subject to definitive agreements and approval by both companies' boards and regulators.

Separately, Chrysler and Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG (BMW) denied a report in The Times of London newspaper (corrects from the New York Times) that the No. 3 U.S. automaker is in talks to buy the Rover small car unit of BMW.
"There is no truth to that," said Chrysler spokesman Mike Aberlich.
He said rumours about Chrysler buying parts of British automaker Rover have surfaced numerous times in the past.
Chrysler officials have been visiting Rover facilities in Britain but the visits are connected to a small-car engine plant that BMW and Chrysler are building in Brazil, he said.
Chrysler's stock rose 31 cents to $34.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
